display.purpose: Page title, usually the account name beside its state pill; 1.5rem below 760px.

headline.purpose: Section and empty-state headings; schedule row times.

stat.purpose: The one big figure in a side panel, such as the next digest time.

title.purpose: Names in lists, settings row titles, rail account names.

bubble.purpose: Digest text inside the bubble; heads and title line at 700.

label.purpose: Field labels and legends; buttons use this size at 500 (primary 600).

caption.purpose: Hints, field errors, meta lines, chips, small buttons.

micro.purpose: Pills, the day chip, table headers, the bubble foot.

mono.purpose: Log lines and inline commands only.

shadows.name: bubble-lift
shadows.purpose: The digest bubble only. --bubble-shadow is rgba(34,49,63,0.08) light, rgba(0,0,0,0.35) dark.

shadows.name: dialog-lift
shadows.purpose: Confirm dialog, over a rgb(21 27 33 / 0.45) backdrop.

shadows.name: tab-underline
shadows.purpose: Current tab marker (slate-ink in dark mode).

motion.name: control
motion.purpose: Background, border and halo changes on buttons, inputs and the switch track.

motion.name: spring
motion.purpose: Bubble arrival (0.32s, 10px rise and fade) and switch knob (0.18s).

motion.name: progress
motion.purpose: Progress bar fill and indeterminate sweep.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion removes every transition and animation.

breakpoints.name: split
breakpoints.purpose: Below: the work split collapses to one column; the side column becomes an auto-fit grid of 240px cards.

breakpoints.name: rail
breakpoints.purpose: Below: the rail becomes a sticky top bar of avatar chips; tabs scroll with an edge fade; settings rows stack.

components.css: .ds-thread { display: grid; gap: 6px; justify-items: start; padding: 16px 16px 16px 24px; background: var(--ground); } .ds-daychip { justify-self: center; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--ink-2); background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 8px; padding: 3px 10px; margin-bottom: 6px; } .ds-bubble { background: var(--bubble); color: var(--ink); border-radius: 4px 18px 18px 18px; padding: 20px 22px 12px; max-width: 680px; width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px var(--bubble-shadow), 0 6px 18px -8px var(--bubble-shadow); display: grid; gap: 14px; line-height: 1.55; font-size: 15px; position: relative; animation: ds-arrive 0.32s cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1); } .ds-bubble::before { content: ""; position: absolute; left: -8px; top: 0; width: 10px; height: 14px; background: var(--bubble); clip-path: polygon(100% 0, 0 0, 100% 100%); } .ds-sec { display: grid; gap: 8px; } .ds-top { gap: 4px; } .ds-b { font-weight: 700; } .ds-sub, .ds-task { color: var(--ink-2); } .ds-task { padding-left: 1.4em; } .ds-foot { display: flex; justify-content: flex-end; gap: 6px; align-items: center; font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--mute); } .ds-num { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-foot svg { stroke: var(--ok); fill: none; stroke-width: 1.8; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; } @keyframes ds-arrive { from { transform: translateY(10px); opacity: 0.4; } to { transform: none; opacity: 1; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-bubble { animation: none; } }

components.css: .ds-switch { position: relative; width: 40px; height: 24px; display: inline-block; } .ds-switch input { position: absolute; inset: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; opacity: 0; margin: 0; cursor: pointer; } .ds-track { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--line-strong); transition: background-color 0.15s ease-out; pointer-events: none; } .ds-track::after { content: ""; position: absolute; top: 3px; left: 3px; width: 18px; height: 18px; border-radius: 50%; background: #fff; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.25); transition: transform 0.18s cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1); } .ds-switch input:checked + .ds-track { background: var(--ok); } .ds-switch input:checked + .ds-track::after { transform: translateX(16px); } .ds-switch input:focus-visible + .ds-track { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
The web is a frame around one message. The digest is drawn exactly as it lands in the account's own chat: a white bubble with a squared top-left corner and a small tail, a day chip above it, the time and delivery ticks in its foot. Everything else on the page (the slate rail of accounts, the tabs, the side column of actions and notices) exists to say whether that message is arriving, to fix it when it is not, and to tune what it says. The system refuses the grey card dashboard where the digest becomes one row of a table.

The material is warm and quiet: a stone-paper ground, hairline warm-grey borders, white surfaces, and one cool slate that does all the structural work (the rail, the primary button, every selected state). Color carries state only. Sea-green means delivered or connected, brick means a problem, ochre means busy or waiting. Density is that of a settings app, not a cockpit: 15px body, generous row padding, one primary action per view.

The whole interface is one system sans, the same face the user's chat client draws in, with tabular numerals wherever a time or a count appears. Nothing loads from the network: the font is the system one and every icon is inline SVG drawn in a single stroke style. Light and dark follow the operating system.
keyCharacteristics: The digest bubble is the one reader everywhere: summary, preview and history run.
A slate rail on the left holds the accounts, each with an avatar initial and a status dot.
Warm stone ground and white surfaces separated by 1px warm-grey hairlines; almost no shadow.
Color is reserved for state: sea-green, brick, ochre, and slate for selection.
One system sans, tabular numerals for times and counts.
Controls share one vocabulary: 10px corners, 1.5px borders, 40 to 44px tall.

rules.name: The State Only Rule
rules.body: Sea-green, brick and ochre appear only when they report a state (delivered, connected, problem, busy). They never decorate, never fill a heading, never become a brand accent.

rules.name: The One Slate Rule
rules.body: Selection, the primary action and the rail all use the same slate. A new selected state uses `primary` on `primary-ink`; it does not introduce a second accent.

rules.name: The Tabular Time Rule
rules.body: Every time, count and number uses tabular numerals (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`): bubble foot, schedule times, table cells, number and time inputs.

rules.name: The Weight Not Face Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is weight and size inside one family. Monospace is for log lines and commands, nothing else.

rules.name: The Problems First Rule
rules.body: In the side column, a problem notice sits above the next-digest panel and the actions. On the accounts home, accounts with problems come first.

rules.name: The One Floating Thing Rule
rules.body: The bubble is the only content that casts a shadow. Panels and cards beside it stay flat, so the message is what the eye lands on.

dos: Do show any digest through the bubble component, with its day chip, time and ticks, wherever a digest appears.
Do use `primary` on `primary-ink` for every selected or current state and for the single primary button of a view.
Do reserve `ok`, `bad` and `warn` for state, each paired with words or an icon so color is never the only signal.
Do keep controls at 10px corners, 1.5px `line-strong` borders, 40px (buttons) or 44px (inputs) tall.
Do separate containers with 1px `line` hairlines on white surfaces; keep them flat.
Do use tabular numerals for every time and count.
Do draw icons as inline 24px-viewbox SVG with a 1.8 stroke, round caps and joins, `currentColor`, no fill.
Do give every interactive element the shared focus ring (2px `focus`, 2px offset) and honor reduced motion, which removes every transition and animation.
Do put the problem notice first in the side column, with its fix action inside the notice.
donts: Don't turn the digest into a row of a table or a grey dashboard card; it is a message in a chat.
Don't load fonts, icon sets or anything else from the network.
Don't add shadows to panels, lists or form sections; the bubble is the only floating content.
Don't introduce a second accent color for selection or emphasis.
Don't render digest text as HTML; it is written by third parties.
Don't use modals except for short confirmations; flows are pages.
